items.title: Geoff Bull Interview, 1966-05-05
items.q: The people who have an image, like Sweet Emma, for instance, because she's had a lot of publicity... I quite like Sweet Emma's playing.

ctx.x: I mean, that, that to me is, the, the fact that people can stand over my, I mean, my idols, if you like to call them that. Mm-hm. I mean, not so much Raymond Burke. The fact that people can tell Jim Robinson and George Lewis and those fellows where they're allowed to or not allowed to play or they're expelled from, from playing at Preservation Hall. And the fact that those same blokes do rely on that place for a living is, to me, a little bit sick. So, in general, my impressions of, of the situation, the way it…
You object to the commercialism of the place, is what you're saying, you know?
